newsitem.title: CHINA: China mulls investing abroad to boost local aviation.
newsitem.headline: China mulls investing abroad to boost local aviation.

text.p: China is negotiating with several countries to invest in local airlines through sales of aircraft produced by its fledgling domestic aviation industry, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

"Many countries are eager to develop their civil aviation industry, the key problem is lack of funds," it quoted Wang Dawei, vice president of China National Aero-Technology Import and Export Corp (CATIC), as saying.
CATIC hoped to sell Chinese-produced aircraft to these airlines, possibly through taking an equity stake or a joint venture, Wang said.
Since 1985, China has signed contracts to sell 82 civil aircraft valued at $250 million, including 69 of its Yun-12 planes, he was quoted as saying.
Market research showed strong demand for China's small planes in Africa, South America and the South Pacific, he said. CATIC was also interested in barter trade, Wang said.

CATIC was already in talks with a private airline in Guinea on swapping shares in the airline for an aircraft, he said. The company had also sent several delegations to the Marshall Islands and Cameroon.
Customers had shown alot of interest in the Yun-12, and Wang said he hoped to see improved sales of the Yun-7 and Yun-8 planes. He gave no details of the size of the aircraft.

CATIC plans to demonstrate a long-distance flight by its Yun-7 and Yun-12 this year in central and western Africa in the second quarter of the year -- China's first such show in the region, Wang said.
While Asia has taken about 60 percent of sales of civilian aircraft by CATIC, great potential was seen in Africa and the South Pacific, Wang said.
